title: Rapid growth is needed, but it must be stable, with sustainable jobs, strong businesses, and fairer welfare.

 Rapid growth is needed, but it must be stable, with sustainable jobs, strong businesses, and fairer welfare.
 Members of Parliament argued that rapid growth must be accompanied by stability, sustainable employment, stronger domestic businesses, and more equitable welfare. The ultimate measure of policy success should not only be the resources mobilized or the targets set, but also the enhancement of domestic production capacity, improved income and quality of life for the people, and a more resilient economy in the face of fluctuations.
 Báo Đại Đoàn Kết • 30/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Manage growth based on realistic scenarios, maintaining macroeconomic stability. 
 National Assembly representative Tran Thi Hong Thanh ( Ninh Binh delegation) stated that while GDP growth in the first nine months was 9.01%, achieving a 10% or higher growth rate for the whole year would require a 12.5% ​​increase in the fourth quarter, a target of 27 out of 34 localities. Therefore, she proposed that the Government quantify the contribution of each driving force, sector, and locality; develop growth and inflation scenarios corresponding to fluctuations in energy prices, interest rates, and international trade; and clearly define risk thresholds and response plans. 
 Ms. Tran Thi Hong Thanh giving a speech (Photo: Quang Vinh) Furthermore, the CPI for the first nine months increased by 4.02%, while real purchasing power only increased by nearly 8%. It is proposed that price management be implemented with a clear roadmap and careful planning, ensuring the supply of essential goods; strictly addressing speculation, hoarding, and price gouging; and providing appropriate support to vulnerable groups, especially low-income earners and workers. Growth targets must be achieved within safe limits, preventing immediate pressures from diminishing the room for maneuver in subsequent years.
 Noting that public investment disbursement in the first nine months reached 62.9% of the plan, Ms. Thanh suggested reviewing each project, clearly identifying obstacles, responsibilities, and the feasibility of completion; reallocating funds from slow-moving projects or those lacking the necessary conditions to projects with high absorption capacity and efficiency. For transportation, electricity, and energy projects, she emphasized the need for synchronized coordination between planning, land acquisition, material sources, transmission grids, connectivity, and power purchase agreements.
 At the same time, it is necessary to finalize the energy reserve strategy early, develop contingency plans for electricity and fuel sources for adverse scenarios; only start large-scale projects when funding sources, schedules, and connectivity are clearly defined; and prevent electricity shortages and infrastructure delays from becoming bottlenecks to growth. 
 Members of Parliament attending the discussion session (Photo: Quang Vinh) Pointing out that exports increased by 24.5% in the first nine months, but imports also increased by 36.7%, resulting in a trade deficit of $19.42 billion; the FDI sector had a trade surplus, while domestic enterprises had a large trade deficit; and the localization rate in some key industries was only about 20%, the delegate from Ninh Binh suggested that FDI attraction policies must be linked to commitments and measurable results regarding technology transfer, human resource training, the level of participation of Vietnamese enterprises, and the enhancement of domestic added value.
 Growth must create more quality jobs and improve living standards. Informal labor still accounts for 61.5%, youth unemployment is at 8.87%, and the poverty reduction target for 2026 has not been met. Delegates proposed linking training with recruitment needs, publicly disclosing employment results after training; focusing on supporting livelihoods and essential services in poor areas and ethnic minority regions; and ensuring that social security policies are not interrupted when integrating national target programs.
 You may also like “We need rapid growth, but at the same time we need stable values, sustainable jobs, strong domestic businesses, and fairer welfare. The ultimate measure of policy is not just the resources mobilized or the targets set, but the enhanced domestic production capacity, improved income and quality of life for the people, and a more resilient economy in the face of fluctuations,” Ms. Thanh said.
 Significant internal challenges 
 According to National Assembly representative Do Duc Minh ( Lao Cai delegation), GDP in the first nine months of the year increased by 9.01%, the highest rate in the past 15 years; import and export turnover exceeded the 1,000 billion USD mark for the first time; macroeconomic stability was maintained; energy security and major economic balances were preserved.
 However, Mr. Minh stated that, looking at the reality, there are significant internal challenges: the domestic business sector is still facing difficulties; the number of businesses withdrawing from the market remains high; exports and imports are heavily dependent on FDI; major economic hubs have not met growth expectations and are under considerable pressure regarding infrastructure and the environment. 
 Mr. Do Duc Minh giving a speech (Photo: Quang Vinh) Based on practical experience, Mr. Minh suggested strengthening institutional reforms and creating breakthroughs in implementation at all levels, coupled with rational resource allocation, to enable localities to proactively implement policies.
 Currently, the Central Government has directed the strengthening of legislative thinking, shifting from pre-approval to post-approval, using the results of serving the people and businesses as a measure. However, in reality, there are still difficulties and obstacles in the implementation of administrative procedures in some areas, and the tendency to shirk responsibility and avoid accountability among some officials remains a problem. Therefore, it is necessary to continue a comprehensive review of the legal system, especially the guiding documents for the implementation of laws and resolutions, to drastically reduce overlapping administrative procedures and business conditions, thereby reducing costs for people and businesses.
 Furthermore, it is necessary to continue implementing synchronized solutions for long-term control and stabilization of input costs in the economy, and to immediately implement strategic autonomy coupled with the completion of the legal framework for essential goods. Accordingly, a comprehensive plan should be developed, clearly assigning responsibilities, timelines, and expected results in ensuring energy, fuel, food, and agricultural supply security, while simultaneously reducing intermediary costs. 
 Delegates attending the discussion session (Photo: Quang Vinh) You may also like At the same time, strengthen economic diplomacy, enhance Vietnam's position in negotiations, and expand cooperation in essential areas. Implement Resolution No. 43 of the National Assembly on reducing personal income tax and corporate income tax promptly, effectively, and appropriately, contributing to stimulating production and consumption and reducing the cost of products and services.
 "The difficulties and challenges ahead are still immense, but with a solid macroeconomic foundation and the strong support and decisive guidance of the political system, I am confident that our country's economy will continue to break through and develop rapidly and sustainably," Mr. Minh said. 
 Anh Vu - Viet Thang - Quang Vinh
